dossier.public_summary: The dip looks deep in one sector (10632 ppm) and much shallower in another (3231 ppm) and the four individual transits are inconsistent, while difference imaging is inconclusive and two nearby stars within a TESS pixel could mimic the dip. A single planet on the target should have the same depth everywhere, so a blended eclipsing binary/variable is the best explanation.

reasons.why: Depth changes 106% between sectors (10632 ppm in sector 67 vs 3231 ppm in sector 92). Single-component tool shows changes_within_a_source cannot be a calibration difference, indicating a blended / variable false positive rather than a planet with one depth.
With 4 transits depths are formally inconsistent, opposite to a planet on a quiet star which should be depth-stable, supporting sector change as astrophysical.

Centroid cannot tie dip to target; neighbours.plausible_within_1px 2 and could_cause_within_1px 3 with closest that could at 1.9 arcsec delta_mag 3.6 eclipse_needed 0.227 remain viable, so off-target eclipse cannot be rejected.
reasons.value: inconclusive, no sector with a clear difference image

reasons.why: Independent classifier rates this as planet-like only 1 in 10 times, consistent with the depth/variability mismatch.
